title: Is Phantom Blade Zero a Soulslike? The Definitive Answer
description: No - Phantom Blade Zero is not a Soulslike, and the developers have said so directly. Here is what it actually is: a fast, parry-driven action game closer to Ninja Gaiden and Devil May Cry.
keyword: is phantom blade zero a soulslike

sections.title: Short Answer: No
sections.content:
Phantom Blade Zero is not a Soulslike. This is not our interpretation - the developer has said it directly.

In an interview with GamesBeat, S-Game founder Soulframe Liang put it plainly:

"Our game is not what we'd precisely label as a Souls or 'Soulslike' game. It's dark. It has some vibes that might make people refer back to that style, but we're not a Souls game."

The reason the question keeps coming up is that the game looks Soulslike in trailers - dark fantasy setting, deliberate combat, punishing bosses, checkpoint-based progression. The resemblance is real, but it is surface level. The mechanics underneath are much closer to character-action games.

sections.title: The Critics Settled It
sections.content:
Before release this question had only the developer's answer and preview impressions. The reviews, published 25-26 October 2026, are consistent, and several critics say it directly:

  • The Outerhaven (10/10): "Soulslike fans should give it a shot too, even though it clearly isn't one."
  • GAMES.CH (85): its reduced reliance on repetitive farming is what "helps it stand out from traditional Soulslikes".
  • PCGamesN (100): describes the structure as "an intricately designed Metroidvania at heart" - which matches what S-GAME has said all along about the world being wide-linear rather than open.
  • VGC (4/5): rates it "undoubtedly stronger than genre stablemates like Black Myth: Wukong" while treating it as its own thing.
  • GameSpot (8/10) and Polygon both frame it as a martial-arts action game first, with GameSpot's headline saying the combat is what carries the story problem.

Two dissenting notes worth keeping, because they are the parts people actually experience as soulslike: Areajugones complains about missing map markers leaving you adrift, and several outlets call the levels linear rather than interconnected - the opposite complaint from the usual open-world one. See the reviews page for the full score list and locations for what is known about the map structure.

sections.title: There Is No Stamina Bar
sections.content:
The single clearest difference: Phantom Blade Zero has no stamina bar in the Souls sense.

Instead it uses the Sha-Chi meter, which behaves quite differently:

ActionEffect on Sha-Chi
Light attacksBuild it
Heavy / special attacksConsume it
BlockingConsumes it
ParryingDoes not consume it
DodgingDoes not consume it at all

That last row matters enormously. In a Souls game, running out of stamina means you cannot dodge and you die. In Phantom Blade Zero you can always dodge, because dodging is free. You can always escape - you just cannot always fight back.

Sha-Chi doubles as a posture-style meter for enemies. Drain an enemy's Sha-Chi completely and they are breached - stance broken and wide open for a finisher.

sections.title: What It Actually Plays Like
sections.content:
The most common comparison from people who have played it is a middle ground between Ninja Gaiden and Sekiro - not one or the other.

Closer to character-action than Souls

  • Combat is fast and combo-heavy rather than patient and deliberate
  • You have two main weapons equipped at once and can switch mid-combo
  • Switching weapons fully restores your Sha-Chi - the core combat loop is build, spend, swap, repeat
  • Flashy, expressive offence is rewarded; turtling behind a shield is not

Closer to Sekiro in one respect

  • Parrying is central, not optional. A perfect parry negates damage and drains the attacker's Sha-Chi
  • There are two attack colours: blue attacks can be blocked or parried, red attacks can only be dodged
  • Both a perfect parry and a perfect dodge trigger Ghoststep - a cinematic reposition that puts Soul behind the enemy for a counter window. Ghoststep changes depending on the weapon you are holding

sections.title: The Main Differences From Souls Games
sections.content:
Phantom Blade ZeroTypical Soulslike
StaminaNo stamina bar; Sha-Chi insteadStamina gates attack and dodge
DodgingFree - never costs resourceCosts stamina
DifficultySelectable modesUsually fixed
BuildsWeapons are the build; no armour setsArmour + stats + gear
ProgressionExplore for upgrade fragments; no stat allocationLevel up and allocate stats
Weapon loadoutTwo mains + two Phantom Edges, swappable mid-comboUsually one weapon at a time

The difficulty point is worth emphasising because it is the least Soulslike thing about the game. Phantom Blade Zero ships with four modes:

  • Wayfarer - for players who want the story
  • Pathbreaker - the standard tier, and the balance the combat was designed around
  • Hellwalker - fighting-game mechanics, bosses that drop preset patterns and adapt
  • 66 Days - Hellwalker intensity plus a 66-death limit; unlocks after finishing on Pathbreaker or Hellwalker

Souls games deliberately refuse to offer this. Phantom Blade Zero does the opposite.

Two mechanics reported from the October 2026 studio preview make the difference concrete rather than a matter of tone: defeated enemies do not simply repopulate when you rest, and death does not leave resources behind to recover. The familiar soulslike escape - farm an area until extra levels carry you through - is therefore not on offer. The intended answer to a wall is a different loadout, more Remnant Dust spent, and reading the fight better.

sections.title: Where the Souls Comparison Is Fair
sections.content:
It is not a baseless comparison. The game does share real DNA with the genre:

  • Checkpoint-based progression with respawning enemies
  • Bosses as the centrepiece - the developer describes boss battles as "the game's highlights" and "the reason you develop your skill and character"
  • Learning attack patterns matters. Per the developer, the main difference between bosses is the rhythm of their blue-eye and red-eye attacks - you learn the pace, parry the blue, dodge the red
  • Deliberately punishing. Previewers have described it as "delightfully punishing"
  • Dark, bleak world. An intentional art direction choice

So if you like Souls games for the boss-focused, pattern-learning, checkpoint-driven structure, you will find a lot to like. If you like them for the stamina management, the build-crafting, or the fixed difficulty, this is a different game.

sections.title: So What Genre Is It?
sections.content:
Phantom Blade Zero is best described as a fast-paced character-action RPG - the umbrella that covers Devil May Cry, Ninja Gaiden and Bayonetta - built around a parry-and-counter core, with light RPG progression layered on.

S-Game's own label for the setting is "KungfuPunk" - traditional wuxia blended with fantasy and folk horror. It is not a Soulslike wearing a wuxia skin.

The practical advice: if you have been avoiding the game because you bounced off Elden Ring, the difficulty modes and the free dodge mean it is far more approachable than it looks. If you have been excited because you want another Souls game, adjust that expectation - but know that the boss design is built to be the main event.

Phantom Blade Zero launches October 29, 2026 on PS5 and PC.
